title: MacNeal and Harder's thick-walled cylinder, nearly incompressible
model: a quarter of a 3.0 bore, 9.0 outside, 1.0 long cylinder on rollers on its symmetry planes and both ends (plane strain), E 1000 and nu 0.49, 0.499 and 0.4999 stated by the study (its units read as mm and MPa), unit pressure in the bore, one study each; 0.5 elements (12 across the wall); the bore's mean radial displacement, from probe_study's rigid fit of the face

u_r_nu_049.source: MacNeal & Harder, A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy, Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3-20, Table 5(c) (thick-walled cylinder, nu = 0.49)
u_r_nu_049.reason: Lame in plane strain, which the paper's value is (0.0050399 by its formula); an element that locks is too stiff as nu nears 1/2 and falls short by far more than its mesh error, and a fully integrated tet10 does not lock: at 12 elements across the wall, as lame_tpu's 10, within half a percent
